Package org.apache.juneau.petstore.console.ops

Class JobsRest

java.lang.Object
jakarta.servlet.GenericServlet
jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServlet
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.servlet.RestServlet
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.servlet.BasicRestServlet
org.apache.juneau.petstore.console.PetstoreConsolePage
org.apache.juneau.petstore.console.ops.JobsRest
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.servlet.Servlet, jakarta.servlet.ServletConfig, Serializable, AsyncJobsMixin, BasicUniversalConfig, DefaultConfig, DefaultHtmlConfig, TerminalMixin
public class JobsRest extends PetstoreConsolePage implements AsyncJobsMixin, TerminalMixin
Jobs: the console's async-job reference. A restock submits once per idempotency key, answers 202 with an AsyncJobRef, and the views runtime follows its streamUrl until the job settles.

The registry de-duplicates on the idempotency key itself (AsyncJobRegistry.tryCreate(IdempotencyKey)), so a resubmit with the same key returns the same job and this resource keeps no key map of its own.

The page's job-log card posts the same restock in its flat form and follows the job's stream. A restock with slowMs waits that long before it touches the store (cancel it then and nothing changes), and every restock holds for holdMs (a second by default) after it has added its pets (cancel it then and the result says the change was made). The registry's hard timeout is 30 s, or whatever a JobsRest.HardTimeout bean on the host says; a JobsRest.GroomPeriod bean sets the groom step and a JobsRest.SpeciesHold bean the species-row hold.

The seeded groom run is created on the first groom request rather than at construction, so a JobsRest.GroomPeriod bean (injected after construction) can set its pace; every groom endpoint goes through it, so the page sees the same data.

The page also hosts the terminal demo: a "groom pet" job (GroomRuns) whose output is served by TerminalMixin and shown two ways — a FreeMarker terminal card over the in-memory output, and a second card over the same run's file-backed transcript.

Example:

// POST /console/ops/jobs/restock {DOG:2, slowMs:3000, holdMs:1000, idempotencyKey:'7f3c...'} var body = Restock.of(json); var job = asyncJobRegistry().tryCreate(IdempotencyKey.of(body.idempotencyKey(), "restock", "restock")).orElse(null); if (job == null) return ActionResult.refusal("app:job-limit"); // answered 429 pool.execute(() -> run(job, body, () -> store().restock(body.perSpecies(), "job:restock"))); return AsyncJobRef.of(job); // answered 202

      public static final String SPECIES_HOLD_PROPERTY
      System property: how long a species row's restock holds after its effect, in milliseconds (default 1000, at most 10000).

      Read on every request, so a test can widen the window in which a cancel lands as cancelled-after-effect. A sample-only knob: the row form never accepts a hold.

    • restockForm

      public ModalDef restockForm()
      The restock dialog's form source: a read-only GET returning the modal with a freshly minted self-targeted key.

      The dialog is the plain restock, so it asks only for counts and always runs with no wait and the default 1000 ms hold. The timing knobs (slowMs, holdMs) belong to the job-log card, which exists to demonstrate cancelling before and after the effect.

      Returns:
      The modal.

    • restockSpecies

      public Object restockSpecies(RestRequest req, RestResponse res, @Path("id") String id, @Content JsonMap json)
      Restocks one species from its row's detail panel.

      The species is the path's {id}, which must equal the body's targetId, which the key must be bound to. The body's fields supply only count; any other field (the panel's hidden species included) is ignored. A replay of a claimed key returns the same job, or a JobKeyLedger.SPENT_CODE refusal once the registry has aged the job out.

      Parameters:
      req - The request.
      res - The response (202, or 409 on a refusal).
      id - The species name.
      json - The action envelope {action, targetId, idempotencyKey, fields:{count}}.
      Returns:
      The job ref (202), a 409 refusal, or a 429 app:job-limit refusal.
      Throws:
      NotFound - If the species is unknown.
      BadRequest - If the envelope is malformed or count is not a whole number 1-50.

    • regroom

      public ActionResult regroom(RestRequest req, RestResponse res, @Path("id") String id, @Content JsonMap json) throws IOException
      Grooms a run's pet again.

      Ledger keys only, bound to the path's run: the pet comes from the server's run record, never the request. /groom stays the dialog's self-targeted endpoint; one endpoint taking both kinds of key would be only as strong as the self-targeted one. A replay returns the same new run while it is kept, then a JobKeyLedger.SPENT_CODE refusal once the run list has evicted it; never a second run.

      Parameters:
      req - The request.
      res - The response (409 on a refusal).
      id - The run id.
      json - The action envelope {action, targetId, idempotencyKey}.
      Returns:
      The new run's row, or a 409 refusal.
      Throws:
      NotFound - If the key is unclaimed and the run is unknown.
      BadRequest - If the envelope is malformed.
      IOException - If the new run's temp file cannot be created.
